If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over last 5 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overconfidence bias.  
If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending down, apply downward bias of 2–3% to mid-horizon (8–15 days) forecasts.  
If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is declining, reduce forecast by 3–5% for late horizon (16–30 days) to reflect bearish momentum.  
If sentiment swings from positive to negative within 3 days, apply a 2–4% downward correction to forecast 10–15 days ahead to account for sentiment reversal.  
If sentiment is uniformly positive but price is flat or slightly rising, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for late horizon to avoid overestimating continuation.  
If sentiment is positive but recent price action shows divergence (e.g., 3-day drop after 5-day rise), apply 1–3% downward adjustment to mid-horizon to correct for sentiment-price mismatch.
